LESSON: FICTION AND NON- FICTION 8.3.1 FICTION: THE PLAY FROM KENYA

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10

Topic 8.3: Fiction and Non- Fiction 8.3.1 Fiction: The Play from Kenya
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Fiction and Non- Fiction 8.3.1 Fiction: The Play from Kenya, part of Strand 8 in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 LITERATURE IN ENGLISH FOR LEARNERS WITH VISUAL IMPAIRMENT JUNE.

Key inquiry question: Why are performance techniques important in a play?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Fiction and Non- Fiction 8.3.1 Fiction: The Play from Kenya together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Learning to learn: This is enhanced as the learner reflects on their learning by work with peers to critique the

performance.

● Creativity and imagination: This is cultivated as the learner applies creative ideas when performing a scene of a play.

Values:
● Respect: This is enhanced as the learner appreciates the input and contributions of peers during the performance.

● Peace: This is developed as the learner harmoniously works with peers to prepare for a performance by rehearsing and

identifying props and costumes.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Social cohesion: This is developed as the learner collaborates with peers to research, prepare and perform a play while

applying performance techniques.
